stem.en: Why is it wrong to call NaCl 'a molecule of salt'?

text.en: The crystal has no separate Na⁺ and Cl⁻ pairs. NaCl gives the 1:1 ratio of its ions.
Salt is a mixture of sodium and chlorine, not a compound.
A molecule must have at least three atoms, and NaCl has only two.

explanation.en: Each Na⁺ is surrounded by six Cl⁻ at the same distance, and each Cl⁻ by six Na⁺, so no pair stands apart from the rest. NaCl is a formula unit: the simplest ratio of the ions. Salt is a compound, not a mixture, because its ions are always in the ratio 1:1. And the number of atoms is not the problem: H₂ has only two atoms and it is a molecule, as we will see in Lesson 11.

hints.en: Picture one Na⁺ in the crystal. Is one of its six Cl⁻ neighbours closer to it than the others?
